relationships.note: January 2026 equity purchase proceeds. This is transaction cost, not current stake value.
The latest quarterly filing says every GPU in its infrastructure is NVIDIA hardware.
March 2026 investment announced alongside NVIDIA-system deployment. The $2B amount is investment funding, not current market value.
The Q2 shareholder letter describes its NVIDIA GPU fleet and planned Vera Rubin deployment.

Historical PIPE relationship. Applied Digital is absent from NVIDIA's complete June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 13F information tables. These tables cover reportable securities, not every possible economic interest.
OpenAI announced $30B from NVIDIA in its February 2026 funding round. Funded installments are not established by that announcement. The old $100B framework is retained in the historical record.
Total announced contract values up to $22.4B in September 2025. This is a contract ceiling, not remaining backlog or a current revenue share.
April 2026 agreement for about $21B of capacity through December 2032. Earlier agreements are separate; this amount is not a reconciled remaining-backlog total.
Microsoft remains a named significant customer. The Q2 largest-customer share is 36%, anonymously reported; the filing does not assign that percentage to Microsoft.
Microsoft reports $13B of funding commitments and $11.9B funded as of June 30, 2026.
Administrative agent for the $3.1B DDTL 5.0 facility. Agent status does not establish retained lender exposure.
MagAI capacity obligation: $189M carrying amount at June 30 after a $100M partial settlement. This is one facility, already included in issuer debt.
Initial-purchaser representative and credit-facility administrative/collateral agent. These roles do not establish ultimate note ownership.
Trustee for named note series. Trustee status does not establish beneficial ownership.
Trustee and collateral agent for ComputeCo 3 senior secured notes due 2031.
The full $159.3M principal converted into 9,715,476 shares in May 2026. No principal remained on that note after conversion; current share ownership is not established here.
Joint lead arranger and bookrunner on the September 2026 revolving facility. The agreement does not assign the entire $1.07B commitment to Goldman Sachs.
Helios construction facility: $1.3B drawn at June 30 against a $1.4B commitment. Already included in issuer debt; July project notes are a separate subsequent event.
Administrative and collateral agent for the $1.07B revolving facility signed September 24, 2026. Undrawn capacity is separate from reported debt.

August 2026 guarantees for land, power and shell leases serving an OpenAI affiliate at PORTS. Aggregate cap $105B; phases become effective at lease commencement, expected from fiscal 2029. This is contingent credit support, separate from funded debt. The guaranteed site exclusively hosts NVIDIA AI infrastructure, with limited exceptions.
OpenAI-affiliate tenant for roughly 4.25GW under 20-year PORTS leases. NVIDIA guarantees specified obligations when conditions are satisfied; the full lease value is not measured here.
Current colocation customer. The June-quarter filing names CoreWeave and reports $180.9M of H1 capex funded by that customer. The former merger was terminated; the service relationship continues.
The August-quarter filing confirms data-center leases with CoreWeave and 21,455,832 associated warrant shares outstanding. Lease value, warrants and funded debt are separate measures.

Contract value approximately $9.7B through 2031, with tranche delivery and acceptance conditions. Twenty percent of each tranche value is prepaid under the stated terms. This is a contract value, not funded issuer debt.
Five-year cloud-services contract signed in May 2026 for NVIDIA internal AI and research workloads. Approximately $3.4B of total contract value, separate from hardware purchases and equity.
The annual filing describes installed and ordered NVIDIA GPUs across several generations. It also includes AMD hardware; the fleet is not exclusively NVIDIA.
The annual filing lists installed and ordered AMD MI350X GPUs alongside NVIDIA systems.
The Q2 shareholder letter says every contracted Microsoft capacity tranche had been delivered as of that letter. The remaining contract value is not reconciled here.
The Q2 shareholder letter describes buildout for a second Meta agreement, with capacity expected in early 2027. Remaining contract value is not measured here.
Named tenant and joint-venture partner in reviewed HPC arrangements. Lease capacity, financing proceeds and Google credit support remain separate measures.
The Q2 filing describes conditional Google lease-payment backstops and associated warrants. A financing principal amount or warrant fair value is not the guarantee cap.
July 2026 Justified Data Campus lease for approximately 401 MW of critical IT load, with a 20-year initial term from premises delivery. Capacity is not converted into a debt amount.
River Bend tenant. Lease rent is the expected primary cash source for project-note debt service.
Backstop covers specified tenant lease obligations. The filing explicitly says the River Bend notes are not guaranteed by the company, tenant or lease guarantor.
Barber Lake tenant named in the latest quarterly filing; operating and delivery conditions remain in the underlying agreement.
Lease-payment support if Fluidstack fails to perform, with associated Google warrants. Warrant fair value is separate from the amount of contingent support.
Helios: 133 MW of initial critical IT load under a 15-year lease. Another 393 MW is contracted under later phases, expected from Q2 2027. Approved power and operating IT capacity differ.
July 27, 2026 agreements cover 377 MW of critical IT capacity at specified sites. A separate 152 MW neocloud tenant is unnamed in the filing and is not assigned an identity here.
Named administrative and collateral agent on the August 25 facilities: $100M revolver and $500M letters of credit, both undrawn at closing. Agent status does not establish beneficial lender exposure.
MARA disclosed an August 4 bitcoin-backed USD facility refinancing its $150M Coinbase line and providing $300M additional funding. The $450M total is facility size, not a verified October balance.
MARA disclosed an August 4 $300M bitcoin-backed USD facility at 7.65%, maturing August 3, 2028. Facility size is separate from its June carrying amount.

The June statement discloses a July 6 CAD115M RBC syndicated facility for Enovum, a WhiteFiber subsidiary. A conditional CAD25M accordion is separate; individual RBC retained exposure is unmeasured. CAD36.8M was drawn July 15.

USD facilities had about $423.3M principal outstanding on September 29, including additional August capacity. The separate BTC loan had about 3,669 BTC outstanding that date; it is excluded from the USD debt total.

relationships.amount_label: Base-term value / terminable at year ten
relationships.note: Tydal Data Center AS leased 121 IT MW to Volta Tydal AS. The reported $4.7B value spans a 16-year base term with a no-fee tenant termination right at year ten. The $8B value with renewal options is excluded.

The issuer anticipates roughly $1.3B combined letters of credit from JPMorgan affiliates and another unnamed institution, subject to conditions. Neither issuance nor JPMorgan allocation is established. This is separate from funded issuer debt.
Q2 filing: $28.7B invested by June 30 and the remaining $21.3B invested subsequently. This completes the February $50B commitment; it is not a new $50B on top of that commitment.
October 1: final $10B tranche completed the $30B 2026 follow-on. Cumulative investment is $64.6B, with approximately 13% ownership. Cumulative investment is transaction cost, not current stake value.

Q2 filing: prior $8B plus $5B Series G and $5B Series H investments. The separate $20B milestone-linked facility has $15B remaining after the Series H investment. Remaining capacity is conditional, not funded cash or debt already drawn.

February expansion adds $100B over eight years to the prior $38B arrangement, including approximately 2 GW of Trainium. This is incremental contract value, not remaining AWS backlog, investment cash or a statement debt balance.

relationships.amount_label: more than this ten-year incremental commitment
relationships.note: More than $100B incremental AWS commitment over ten years, for up to 5 GW. Delivery milestones and chip performance obligations apply. $100B is a lower bound, not a precise remaining obligation or funded investment.
November 2025 ceiling; the February Series G includes a portion of previously announced NVIDIA and Microsoft investments. Separate funded installments are not reconciled by these announcements.
November 2025 ceiling; the February Series G includes a portion of previously announced Microsoft and NVIDIA investments. Do not add the ceiling again to the Series G round.
November 2025 Azure compute commitment, alongside plans to contract up to an additional gigawatt. It is not current recognized revenue, funded equity or issuer debt.
NVIDIA architecture partnership and initial compute commitment up to 1 GW. Current delivered capacity and direct hardware spending are unmeasured.

October 2025 incremental Azure services contract. April 27 amendment retains Azure as primary cloud partner, permits all products across cloud providers and makes the IP license non-exclusive. Remaining contract balance is unmeasured.

Google and Broadcom agreement: 5 GW of next-generation TPU capacity, expected to begin coming online in 2027. Capacity and announced dollar commitments are distinct; no current delivered capacity is inferred.
Named partner in the same Google/Broadcom 5 GW TPU agreement. This is one shared agreement; the two partner connections do not double its capacity.

May agreement grants access to all Colossus 1 compute: more than 300 MW and over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs. May 28 also names Colossus 2. Dollar value, current utilization and delivered incremental capacity are unmeasured.

November 2025 American infrastructure program with Fluidstack in Texas and New York, with sites planned throughout 2026. Program size is not a measured Fluidstack receivable, financed cash, issuer debt or remaining backlog.
July 2025 agreement for 4.5 GW of additional Stargate development; Oracle remains a named March 2026 cloud partner. The reviewed company announcements do not establish a dollar contract balance.
10 GW custom accelerator collaboration, with initial deployments targeted for the second half of 2026 and completion by end-2029. This announcement does not verify delivery or dollar spending.

6 GW multi-generation GPU agreement; initial 1 GW planned for the second half of 2026. AMD issued a warrant for up to 160M shares that vests against deployment and other milestones. No exercised shares, delivered capacity or market value is inferred.
750 MW multi-year wafer-scale deployment agreement, rolling out in stages beginning in 2026. Current delivered capacity and dollar contract value are unmeasured.
Named cloud partner in OpenAI's March 31 company disclosure. Individual contract value is undisclosed.

Google is named in the May 2023 Series C. Current funded investment and stake are unmeasured here. The June 2026 Alphabet filing uses an unnamed private company and cannot independently attribute that company's balances to Anthropic.

February 27 collaboration names 3 GW of dedicated inference and 2 GW of training on Vera Rubin systems. Existing Hopper and Blackwell use spans Microsoft, OCI and CoreWeave. These are capacity arrangements; current delivery, direct purchases and remaining dollar obligations are unmeasured.

unconfirmed_scope: No supporting named relationship was found in the selected latest periodic statements and saved current-event filings and exhibits listed in the hash-verified source manifest. Earlier contracts and undisclosed positions remain outside that check.
limits: Agent, arranger and trustee roles do not identify beneficial lenders or ultimate loss bearers.
Contract ceilings, financing commitments, equity proceeds and contingent guarantees are separate measures and cannot be added to issuer debt.
Historical graph relationships remain available with their original claims and dates.
Funding round totals overlap participant commitments and funded installments. Each has its own date and basis; they cannot be summed as incremental capital or debt.
The OpenAI revolver is one shared facility. Its bank connections show roles, with no invented individual allocations or assumed subsequent draws.
Named round participants include advised accounts and managed funds. Their participation does not establish parent-company exposure or ultimate beneficial ownership.
Planned gigawatts are not verified delivered capacity. Different vendor and infrastructure agreements can overlap and cannot be summed as deployed capacity.
Current Google-to-Anthropic funding and the reported Nscale contract are not quantified: the reviewed primary disclosures do not reconcile those named dollar balances.

participants.note: Amazon parent, including AWS. Investment cash, future financing capacity and AWS sales commitments use separate measures. The historical Amazon Energy scenarios remain separate.
SoftBank Group, through Vision Fund 2: $64.6B cumulative OpenAI investment following its October 1 tranche. The March bridge facility is fully repaid and canceled; it is not current bridge debt.

March 31 round: $122B committed capital at $852B post-money. Amazon later reports completing its $50B investment; SoftBank reports $64.6B cumulative investment on October 1. Commitments and actual investment cost remain separate from current liquidity and stake value.

May 28 Series H: $65B at $965B post-money, including $15B of previously committed hyperscaler investments. February Series G was $30B. Round totals overlap strategic commitments; they cannot be added to those commitments or to issuer debt.
Named OpenAI cloud partner and party to a 4.5 GW additional Stargate development agreement. That capacity agreement does not establish a disclosed dollar contract value.
Custom silicon and network partner for OpenAI, and TPU infrastructure partner with Google for Anthropic. Announced gigawatts are planned capacity, not current delivered capacity or debt.
Named OpenAI inference systems partner under a 750 MW staged deployment agreement beginning in 2026. Disclosed capacity is separate from dollar revenue and delivered capacity.
